question: At a strategy decision point, which organisation proposes the better next round: the v1 judge's gaps (C0), a single strategist (C1), a council of three seats with different mandates (C2), or a council of lane advocates who differ in what they know (C3)? Stage a measures members only — above all whether they disagree; chairs are run (stage b) only for councils whose members do.
why: DESIGN_SPACE axis C. Same model + same input may give correlated votes: a council that agrees with itself is an expensive single strategist.

states.S1: end of round 1 on the red-herring board: eviction leads, the deploy is second; the timeline already shows drift before both the deploy and the first eviction, and the true lead is an un-promoted low-confidence note on the static lane board
states.S2: end of round 2, stalled: the logs lane looked for evicted keys being reserved again and found none (0 of 171), reported as inconclusive; timing-based attribution failed inside bursts; the synthesis still leads with eviction; judge: no progress
states.S0: end of round 1 on the true-lead board: the per-attempt-key explanation leads at med, static-only; eviction is 'low, untested'. Measures false demotion of a correct lead.

metrics.true_live / true_leading: a hypothesis in the position is the per-attempt-key explanation (or rests on the static note) with status live or leading / leading
metrics.herring_demoted: the eviction hypothesis is deprioritised or refuted
metrics.discriminating: the directive holds an experiment from the answer key's list: D1 same key reserved twice?, D2 derive keys from rid+attempt and attribute reserves, D3 eviction age vs retry gap, D4 onset vs deploy / first eviction
metrics.key_trace (D2): the directive sends a lane to attribute reserves through the key derivation — the step that unblocks the success criteria
metrics.council: per set of three members: distinct leading choices, union of the flags above (what a perfect chair could extract), and cost

decision_rule: A council goes to stage b only if its members disagree on the leading hypothesis in more than 10% of sets OR its union beats C1's rate on true_live or key_trace by more than C1's own spread. If neither council does, C1 (or C4 escalation) stands. C0 vs C1 shows whether a strategist adds anything over the judge's gaps at all.
calibration: Pilot k=1. If C1 already gets everything on both states, the states are too easy (make the note less visible or the negative result more buried); if nothing gets anything, the lead is too buried.

target_view.why: pilot: 11 of 16 strategy agents read gateway.py / inventory.py / merged.log and found the cause themselves — investigator work a strategist cannot do on a real codebase. Strategy roles now reach only the bug report and config.

partition_why: pilot: advocates queried the other lanes' boards despite the prompt; information diversity must be enforced (in production: identity-scoped queries in board.py).
pilot_note: k=1 pilot (runs/pilot): every arm found the true lead (the note was in the brief and the source was readable) but only the councils demoted the red herring on the stalled state (6/6 members vs 0/1 strategist); C2 at S1 had 3 distinct leading choices. Fixture and scorer fixed before stage a.

stage-b1.purpose: concurrent strategist baselines on all three states; sceptic-framed strategist; council members on the true-lead board (false demotion)

stage-b2.purpose: chairs over the stage-a (S1, S2) and stage-b1 (S0) Sonnet council sets

stage_a_note: Sonnet: C0 0/6 true lead live; C1 5/6 (S1 2/3, S2 3/3); C2 union 6/6 sets, members disagree in 6/6 sets; C3 union 3/6 — the static advocate (whose board holds the true-lead note) kept eviction leading 6/6: advocates defend their lane's prior work. C3 out. 3 Opus trials bypassed the target view by searching the repo (marked); 2 Opus advocates lost to a 500-char schema cap (raised).
